en: Subsidies, taxes, and regulations / can all lead to power plants that pollute less / by switching away from coal. / In all cases, profits can be ① higher / from making the transition, / even taking the related costs into account. Even if we take the related costs into account → Even taking the related costs into account The power plants prefer subsidies / over regulations or taxes. / The reason is ② obvious. / They prefer to receive money from the government / rather than pay the costs themselves.

A subsidy that cuts pollution per unit can still increase pollution overall. subsidies / has to be matched / by the contraction of the opportunity set of others. / The electricity companies' "freedom" is ③ decreased / at the expense of the ordinary individual, / who must suffer from increased taxation / to pay for the subsidy. Moreover, from the perspective of pure efficiency, / the subsidy ④ distorts the economy / because the electricity company is not facing / the full costs of what it does, / even if it is successful in limiting emissions. Indeed, electricity prices may end up ⑤ lower / than they should be / and electricity consumption higher, / which will worsen global warming, / even though the emissions per unit of electricity / have been reduced. Also, In addition, Additionally, Furthermore, Moreover, What's more,
Power plants prefer subsidies for switching away from coal, but subsidies shift the costs to taxpayers and keep electricity prices too low, which can increase consumption and worsen global warming.
